docs.title: Postcode-SIMD column provenance
docs.text:
For every column of the two tables, where its value comes from, what was done to it, how the build checks it, and why: follow a column to its pinned source file and the decision behind it.

Generated from commit 2c52f54: package 6.0.0; schemas postcode_simd_wide_v5 (history) and postcode_simd_sspl_v5 (main); SPD 2026/2, SSPL 2026/2. Metadata only: no data values.

  • Columns: one page per column name, each table's provenance side by side where they differ
  • Pinned sources: every published file the build reads, and the columns it feeds
  • Decisions: why each column is made the way it is
  • Checks: what each build check tests

docs.title: Review status
docs.text: Descriptions extracted from the pinned NRS dictionaries (69): 67 approved, 2 corrected and awaiting confirmation, 0 not yet reviewed. From the SIMD 2020v2 glossary (48): 48 approved, 0 corrected and awaiting confirmation, 0 not yet reviewed; The SIMD glossary describes the 2020v2 shapefile. Its approval covers 2020v2 only: on an earlier edition's page its descriptions are 2020v2 examples, not a verification of that edition's indicators. Reviews: Codex (AI-assisted editorial review), 2026-10-02, record. Each page states the review status of its text.

docs.text:
NRS data dictionary (extracted; corrected after review (AI-assisted review, 2026-10-02, record); awaiting confirmation)

Dictionary table Type Range Description spd small user (spd-indexdatadictionary-2026-2.docx) Char(1) 1 to 8 Indicates the positional accuracy of the GridLink grid reference allocated to each postcode. Description of status values 1. Automatically calculated to be within the building of the matched address closest to the postcode. 2. As for status value 1, except by visual inspection of OS MasterMap® Topography Layer maps. 3. Approximate to within 50 m of true position. 4. Postcode unit mean – (mean of matched addresses with the same postcode, but not snapped to a building). 5. Postcode imputed by ONS by reference to surrounding known postcodes. 6. Postcode sector mean – mainly PO boxes. 7. Postcode terminated. The accuracy of the data is as indicated by its status value immediately prior to its termination. 8. No coordinates available. Note that grid references for PO Box postcodes are assigned to the local Royal Mail sorting/delivery office and are deemed low quality. docs.text:
Where it comes from

Input Field Condition Reaches the row by SPD/spd_postcodeindex_cut_26_2_csv/SmallUser.csv (pinned, SHA256 fc82f1091ac1…) DateOfDeletion the row itself SPD/spd_postcodeindex_cut_26_2_csv/LargeUser.csv (pinned, SHA256 dcb060cbce01…) DateOfDeletion the row itself

Scope: the row itself.

What was done to it: parsed. DateOfDeletion parsed as a date; null while the record is current. (code: simd_ingest/core/spd.py)

How it is checked (what each check tests; whether a build passed it is in that build's manifest.json["checks"])

  • spd.primary_key_unique: the key (pc_norm, introduced_on) is unique and never null
  • spd.primary_key_nonnull: the key (pc_norm, introduced_on) is unique and never null
  • readback.history.index_columns: the saved file's NRS columns equal the source, re-read

Why: half-open-intervals

docs.title: simd2004_access_domain_decile
docs.text:
Scottish Government SIMD 2004 access domain decile, unweighted, 1 = most deprived; copied exactly as published on statistics.gov.scot, never derived; the publisher places some tied zones in adjacent bands

What the access domain measures (indicators in the Scottish Government's SIMD 2020v2 glossary; earlier editions' indicators differ in detail):

  • Average drive time to a petrol station in minutes (GAccPetrol, time (minutes); SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)
  • Average drive time to a GP surgery in minutes (GAccDTGP, time (minutes); SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)
  • Average drive time to a post office in minutes (GAccDTPost, time (minutes); SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)
  • Average drive time to a primary school in minutes (GAccDTPsch, time (minutes); SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)
  • Average drive time to a secondary school in minutes (GAccDTSsch, time (minutes); SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)
  • Average drive time to a retail centre in minutes (GAccDTRet, time (minutes); SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)
  • Public transport travel time to a GP surgery in minutes (GAccPTGP, time (minutes); SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)
  • Public transport travel time to a post office in minutes (GAccPTPost, time (minutes); SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)
  • Public transport travel time to a retail centre in minutes (GAccPTRet, time (minutes); SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)
  • Percentage of premises without access to superfast broadband (at least 30Mb/s download speed) (GAccBrdbnd, percentage; SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)

SIMD 2004 education domain, Scotland quintile, 1 = most deprived. Computed population-weighted band, using a midpoint rule validated against PHS's published overall bands; equal ranks grouped together; not published by PHS or the Government

What the education domain measures (indicators in the Scottish Government's SIMD 2020v2 glossary; earlier editions' indicators differ in detail):

  • School pupil attendance (EduAttend, percentage; SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)
  • Attainment of school leavers (EduAttain, score; SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)
  • Working age people with no qualifications (EduNoQuals, standardised ratio; SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)
  • Proportion of people aged 16-19 not participating in education, employment or training (EduNotPart, percentage; SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)
  • 17-21 year olds entering university as a proportion of the 17-21 population (EduUniver, percentage; SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)
Table Type Nullable Category In the CSV export SQL Server type history table (postcode_simd_history, SPD) int8 no computed population-weighted domain band yes tinyint main table (postcode_simd, SSPL) int8 no computed population-weighted domain band yes tinyint

docs.title: Provenance (the same in both tables)
docs.text:
Each table runs its own copy of the table-level checks, named .history. and .main..

Where it comes from

Input Field Condition Reaches the row by data.gov.uk/SG_SIMD_2004/SG_SIMD_2004.dbf (pinned, SHA256 8a17b1aa0df6…) edurank every data zone of the edition DataZone2001Code = datazone data.gov.uk/SG_SIMD_2004/SG_SIMD_2004.dbf (pinned, SHA256 8a17b1aa0df6…) totpop2001 every data zone of the edition DataZone2001Code = datazone

Scope: every data zone of SIMD 2004, once, with its population; never the table's rows.

What was done to it: computed. Zones ordered by the domain rank, equal ranks one block; band = max(1, min(5, ceil(midpoint x 5 / total))), where midpoint is the cumulative population through the block minus half the block's. Computed, not published. (code: simd_ingest/core/weighted.py: population_bands)

How it is checked (what each check tests; whether a build passed it is in that build's manifest.json["checks"])

  • weighted.2004.zones: the population is joined to every PHS zone of the edition
  • weighted.2004.reproduces_phs_scotland_quintile: the population midpoint rule reproduces PHS's published overall Scotland band on every zone
  • join.<table>.simd2004_education_domain_pw_scotland_quintile.range: every joined band is within its range
  • readback.<table>.attached_values: every attached value in the saved file is looked up again from the sources and equal

Why: computed-weighted-domain-bands

docs.title: Provenance (the same in both tables)
docs.text:
Each table runs its own copy of the table-level checks, named .history. and .main..

Where it comes from

Input Field Condition Reaches the row by statistics.gov.scot/simd_historical_2004_2012.csv (pinned, SHA256 d9745d9d7763…) Value SIMD Domain = Education Skills And Training, Measurement = Quintile, DateCode = 2004 DataZone2001Code = FeatureCode data.gov.uk/SG_SIMD_2004/SG_SIMD_2004.dbf (pinned, SHA256 8a17b1aa0df6…) edurank the rank the published rank must equal, or differ from as declared DataZone2001Code = datazone

Scope: the row itself.

What was done to it: copied (gated). The Scottish Government's published band, copied, never derived; admitted only where the published rank is the shapefile's, a half the dataset rounds up allowed. (code: simd_ingest/core/govscot.py: read_published_bands)

  • govscot.2004.bands.education.zones: every zone of the edition is published once for the domain
  • govscot.2004.bands.education.ranks_agree: every published rank equals the shapefile rank, or differs only in a declared way
  • join.<table>.gov.2004.every_record_matched: every record found its data zone in the edition: no empty cell
  • readback.<table>.attached_values: every attached value in the saved file is looked up again from the sources and equal
  • govscot.2004.bands.education.quintile.whole: every published band is a whole number
  • govscot.2004.bands.education.quintile.range: every published band is within its range
  • govscot.2004.bands.education.quintile.monotone: the published band never falls as the published rank rises (a split tie is allowed)
  • join.<table>.simd2004_education_domain_quintile.range: every joined band is within its range

Why: simd-domain-bands, bands-are-looked-up

SIMD 2004 housing domain, Scotland quintile, 1 = most deprived. Computed population-weighted band, using a midpoint rule validated against PHS's published overall bands; equal ranks grouped together; not published by PHS or the Government

What the housing domain measures (indicators in the Scottish Government's SIMD 2020v2 glossary; earlier editions' indicators differ in detail):

  • Number of people in households that are overcrowded (HouseNumOC, count; SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)
  • Number of people in households without central heating (HouseNumNC, count; SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)
  • Percentage of people in households that are overcrowded (HouseOCrat, percentage; SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)
  • Percentage of people in households without central heating (HouseNCrat, percentage; SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)
Table Type Nullable Category In the CSV export SQL Server type history table (postcode_simd_history, SPD) int8 no computed population-weighted domain band yes tinyint main table (postcode_simd, SSPL) int8 no computed population-weighted domain band yes tinyint

docs.title: Provenance (the same in both tables)
docs.text:
Each table runs its own copy of the table-level checks, named .history. and .main..

Where it comes from

Input Field Condition Reaches the row by data.gov.uk/SG_SIMD_2004/SG_SIMD_2004.dbf (pinned, SHA256 8a17b1aa0df6…) houserank every data zone of the edition DataZone2001Code = datazone data.gov.uk/SG_SIMD_2004/SG_SIMD_2004.dbf (pinned, SHA256 8a17b1aa0df6…) totpop2001 every data zone of the edition DataZone2001Code = datazone

Scope: every data zone of SIMD 2004, once, with its population; never the table's rows.

What was done to it: computed. Zones ordered by the domain rank, equal ranks one block; band = max(1, min(5, ceil(midpoint x 5 / total))), where midpoint is the cumulative population through the block minus half the block's. Computed, not published. (code: simd_ingest/core/weighted.py: population_bands)

How it is checked (what each check tests; whether a build passed it is in that build's manifest.json["checks"])

  • weighted.2004.zones: the population is joined to every PHS zone of the edition
  • weighted.2004.reproduces_phs_scotland_quintile: the population midpoint rule reproduces PHS's published overall Scotland band on every zone
  • join.<table>.simd2004_housing_domain_pw_scotland_quintile.range: every joined band is within its range
  • readback.<table>.attached_values: every attached value in the saved file is looked up again from the sources and equal

Why: computed-weighted-domain-bands

docs.title: Provenance (the same in both tables)
docs.text:
Each table runs its own copy of the table-level checks, named .history. and .main..

Where it comes from

Input Field Condition Reaches the row by statistics.gov.scot/simd_historical_2004_2012.csv (pinned, SHA256 d9745d9d7763…) Value SIMD Domain = Housing, Measurement = Quintile, DateCode = 2004 DataZone2001Code = FeatureCode data.gov.uk/SG_SIMD_2004/SG_SIMD_2004.dbf (pinned, SHA256 8a17b1aa0df6…) houserank the rank the published rank must equal, or differ from as declared DataZone2001Code = datazone

Scope: the row itself.

What was done to it: copied (gated). The Scottish Government's published band, copied, never derived; admitted only where the published rank is the shapefile's, a half the dataset rounds up allowed. (code: simd_ingest/core/govscot.py: read_published_bands)

How it is checked (what each check tests; whether a build passed it is in that build's manifest.json["checks"])

  • govscot.2004.bands.years: the band file holds exactly the years the registry declares for it
  • govscot.2004.bands.housing.zones: every zone of the edition is published once for the domain
  • govscot.2004.bands.housing.ranks_agree: every published rank equals the shapefile rank, or differs only in a declared way
  • join.<table>.gov.2004.every_record_matched: every record found its data zone in the edition: no empty cell
  • readback.<table>.attached_values: every attached value in the saved file is looked up again from the sources and equal
  • govscot.2004.bands.housing.quintile.whole: every published band is a whole number
  • govscot.2004.bands.housing.quintile.range: every published band is within its range
  • govscot.2004.bands.housing.quintile.monotone: the published band never falls as the published rank rises (a split tie is allowed)
  • join.<table>.simd2004_housing_domain_quintile.range: every joined band is within its range

Why: simd-domain-bands, bands-are-looked-up

docs.title: simd2006_crime_domain_pw_scotland_decile
docs.text:
SIMD 2006 crime domain, Scotland decile, 1 = most deprived. Computed population-weighted band, using a midpoint rule validated against PHS's published overall bands; equal ranks grouped together; not published by PHS or the Government

What the crime domain measures (indicators in the Scottish Government's SIMD 2020v2 glossary; earlier editions' indicators differ in detail):

  • Number of recorded crimes of violence, sexual offences, domestic housebreaking, vandalism, drugs offences, and common assault (CrimeCount, count; SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)
  • Recorded crimes of violence, sexual offences, domestic housebreaking, vandalism, drugs offences, and common assault per 10,000 population (CrimeRate, rate; SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)
Table Type Nullable Category In the CSV export SQL Server type history table (postcode_simd_history, SPD) int8 no computed population-weighted domain band yes tinyint main table (postcode_simd, SSPL) int8 no computed population-weighted domain band yes tinyint

docs.title: simd2009v2_access_domain_decile
docs.text:
Scottish Government SIMD 2009v2 access domain decile, unweighted, 1 = most deprived; copied exactly as published on statistics.gov.scot, never derived; the publisher places some tied zones in adjacent bands

What the access domain measures (indicators in the Scottish Government's SIMD 2020v2 glossary; earlier editions' indicators differ in detail):

  • Average drive time to a petrol station in minutes (GAccPetrol, time (minutes); SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)
  • Average drive time to a GP surgery in minutes (GAccDTGP, time (minutes); SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)
  • Average drive time to a post office in minutes (GAccDTPost, time (minutes); SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)
  • Average drive time to a primary school in minutes (GAccDTPsch, time (minutes); SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)
  • Average drive time to a secondary school in minutes (GAccDTSsch, time (minutes); SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)
  • Average drive time to a retail centre in minutes (GAccDTRet, time (minutes); SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)
  • Public transport travel time to a GP surgery in minutes (GAccPTGP, time (minutes); SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)
  • Public transport travel time to a post office in minutes (GAccPTPost, time (minutes); SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)
  • Public transport travel time to a retail centre in minutes (GAccPTRet, time (minutes); SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)
  • Percentage of premises without access to superfast broadband (at least 30Mb/s download speed) (GAccBrdbnd, percentage; SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)

What the income domain measures (indicators in the Scottish Government's SIMD 2020v2 glossary; earlier editions' indicators differ in detail):

  • Percentage of people who are income deprived (IncRate, percentage; SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)

docs.text:

Where it comes from

Input Field Condition Reaches the row by data.gov.uk/SG_SIMD_2009/SG_SIMD_2009.dbf (pinned, SHA256 6dde46887ba7…) incrank every data zone of the edition DataZone2001Code = datazone data.gov.uk/SG_SIMD_2009/SG_SIMD_2009.dbf (pinned, SHA256 6dde46887ba7…) sape2007 every data zone of the edition DataZone2001Code = datazone

Scope: every data zone of SIMD 2009v2, once, with its population; never the table's rows.

What was done to it: computed. Zones ordered by the domain rank, equal ranks one block; band = max(1, min(10, ceil(midpoint x 10 / total))), where midpoint is the cumulative population through the block minus half the block's. Computed, not published. (code: simd_ingest/core/weighted.py: population_bands)

How it is checked (what each check tests; whether a build passed it is in that build's manifest.json["checks"])

  • weighted.2009v2.zones: the population is joined to every PHS zone of the edition
  • weighted.2009v2.reproduces_phs_scotland_decile: the population midpoint rule reproduces PHS's published overall Scotland band on every zone
  • join.<table>.simd2009v2_income_domain_pw_scotland_decile.range: every joined band is within its range
  • readback.<table>.attached_values: every attached value in the saved file is looked up again from the sources and equal

Why: computed-weighted-domain-bands

docs.title: simd2012_access_domain_decile
docs.text:
Scottish Government SIMD 2012 access domain decile, unweighted, 1 = most deprived; copied exactly as published on statistics.gov.scot, never derived; the publisher places some tied zones in adjacent bands

What the access domain measures (indicators in the Scottish Government's SIMD 2020v2 glossary; earlier editions' indicators differ in detail):

  • Average drive time to a petrol station in minutes (GAccPetrol, time (minutes); SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)
  • Average drive time to a GP surgery in minutes (GAccDTGP, time (minutes); SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)
  • Average drive time to a post office in minutes (GAccDTPost, time (minutes); SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)
  • Average drive time to a primary school in minutes (GAccDTPsch, time (minutes); SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)
  • Average drive time to a secondary school in minutes (GAccDTSsch, time (minutes); SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)
  • Average drive time to a retail centre in minutes (GAccDTRet, time (minutes); SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)
  • Public transport travel time to a GP surgery in minutes (GAccPTGP, time (minutes); SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)
  • Public transport travel time to a post office in minutes (GAccPTPost, time (minutes); SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)
  • Public transport travel time to a retail centre in minutes (GAccPTRet, time (minutes); SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)
  • Percentage of premises without access to superfast broadband (at least 30Mb/s download speed) (GAccBrdbnd, percentage; SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)

docs.title: simd2012_access_domain_pw_scotland_decile
docs.text:
SIMD 2012 access domain, Scotland decile, 1 = most deprived. Computed population-weighted band, using a midpoint rule validated against PHS's published overall bands; equal ranks grouped together; not published by PHS or the Government

What the access domain measures (indicators in the Scottish Government's SIMD 2020v2 glossary; earlier editions' indicators differ in detail):

docs.title: simd2016_access_domain_decile
docs.text:
Scottish Government SIMD 2016 access domain decile, unweighted, 1 = most deprived; copied exactly as published on statistics.gov.scot, never derived; the publisher places some tied zones in adjacent bands

What the access domain measures (indicators in the Scottish Government's SIMD 2020v2 glossary; earlier editions' indicators differ in detail):

  • Average drive time to a petrol station in minutes (GAccPetrol, time (minutes); SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)
  • Average drive time to a GP surgery in minutes (GAccDTGP, time (minutes); SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)
  • Average drive time to a post office in minutes (GAccDTPost, time (minutes); SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)
  • Average drive time to a primary school in minutes (GAccDTPsch, time (minutes); SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)
  • Average drive time to a secondary school in minutes (GAccDTSsch, time (minutes); SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)
  • Average drive time to a retail centre in minutes (GAccDTRet, time (minutes); SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)
  • Public transport travel time to a GP surgery in minutes (GAccPTGP, time (minutes); SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)
  • Public transport travel time to a post office in minutes (GAccPTPost, time (minutes); SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)
  • Public transport travel time to a retail centre in minutes (GAccPTRet, time (minutes); SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)
  • Percentage of premises without access to superfast broadband (at least 30Mb/s download speed) (GAccBrdbnd, percentage; SIMD 2020v2 glossary: a 2020v2 example, not verified for this edition)

docs.text:

  • Average drive time to a primary school in minutes (GAccDTPsch, time (minutes); SIMD 2020v2 glossary; reviewed (AI-assisted review, 2026-10-02, record))
  • Average drive time to a secondary school in minutes (GAccDTSsch, time (minutes); SIMD 2020v2 glossary; reviewed (AI-assisted review, 2026-10-02, record))
  • Average drive time to a retail centre in minutes (GAccDTRet, time (minutes); SIMD 2020v2 glossary; reviewed (AI-assisted review, 2026-10-02, record))
  • Public transport travel time to a GP surgery in minutes (GAccPTGP, time (minutes); SIMD 2020v2 glossary; reviewed (AI-assisted review, 2026-10-02, record))
  • Public transport travel time to a post office in minutes (GAccPTPost, time (minutes); SIMD 2020v2 glossary; reviewed (AI-assisted review, 2026-10-02, record))
  • Public transport travel time to a retail centre in minutes (GAccPTRet, time (minutes); SIMD 2020v2 glossary; reviewed (AI-assisted review, 2026-10-02, record))
  • Percentage of premises without access to superfast broadband (at least 30Mb/s download speed) (GAccBrdbnd, percentage; SIMD 2020v2 glossary; reviewed (AI-assisted review, 2026-10-02, record))

Scottish Government SIMD 2020v2 employment domain quintile, unweighted, 1 = most deprived; copied exactly as published on statistics.gov.scot, never derived; the publisher places some tied zones in adjacent bands

What the employment domain measures (indicators in the Scottish Government's SIMD 2020v2 glossary; earlier editions' indicators differ in detail):

  • Percentage of working age people who are employment deprived (EmpRate, percentage; SIMD 2020v2 glossary; reviewed (AI-assisted review, 2026-10-02, record))
  • Number of working age people who are employment deprived (EmpNumDep, count; SIMD 2020v2 glossary; reviewed (AI-assisted review, 2026-10-02, record))
Table Type Nullable Category In the CSV export SQL Server type history table (postcode_simd_history, SPD) int8 no Scottish Government published domain band yes tinyint main table (postcode_simd, SSPL) int8 no Scottish Government published domain band yes tinyint

docs.title: Provenance (the same in both tables)
docs.text:
Each table runs its own copy of the table-level checks, named .history. and .main..

Where it comes from

Input Field Condition Reaches the row by statistics.gov.scot/simd_2020.csv (pinned, SHA256 25fea7ddaf54…) Value SIMD Domain = Employment, Measurement = Quintile, DateCode = 2020 DataZone2011Code = FeatureCode data.gov.uk/SG_SIMD_2020/SG_SIMD_2020.dbf (pinned, SHA256 3eb0f27aa4aa…) emprank: Employment domain rank (SIMD 2020v2 glossary; reviewed (AI-assisted review, 2026-10-02, record)) the rank the published rank must equal, or differ from as declared DataZone2011Code = datazone

Scope: the row itself.

What was done to it: copied (gated). The Scottish Government's published band, copied, never derived; admitted only where the published rank is the shapefile's. (code: simd_ingest/core/govscot.py: read_published_bands)

How it is checked (what each check tests; whether a build passed it is in that build's manifest.json["checks"])

  • source.hash.statistics.gov.scot/simd_2020.csv: the pinned file's SHA256 equals the registry's: the bytes are exactly the ones reviewed
  • govscot.2020v2.bands.years: the band file holds exactly the years the registry declares for it
  • govscot.2020v2.bands.employment.zones: every zone of the edition is published once for the domain
  • govscot.2020v2.bands.employment.ranks_agree: every published rank equals the shapefile rank, or differs only in a declared way
  • join.<table>.gov.2020v2.every_record_matched: every record found its data zone in the edition: no empty cell
  • readback.<table>.attached_values: every attached value in the saved file is looked up again from the sources and equal
  • govscot.2020v2.bands.employment.quintile.whole: every published band is a whole number
  • govscot.2020v2.bands.employment.quintile.range: every published band is within its range
  • govscot.2020v2.bands.employment.quintile.monotone: the published band never falls as the published rank rises (a split tie is allowed)
  • join.<table>.simd2020v2_employment_domain_quintile.range: every joined band is within its range

Why: simd-domain-bands, bands-are-looked-up

docs.title: simd2020v2_health_domain_pw_scotland_decile
docs.text:

What the health domain measures (indicators in the Scottish Government's SIMD 2020v2 glossary; earlier editions' indicators differ in detail):

  • Comparative illness factor (HlthCIFSR, standardised ratio; SIMD 2020v2 glossary; reviewed (AI-assisted review, 2026-10-02, record))
  • Hospital stays related to alcohol use (HlthAlcSR, standardised ratio; SIMD 2020v2 glossary; reviewed (AI-assisted review, 2026-10-02, record))
  • Hospital stays related to drug use (HlthDrugSR, standardised ratio; SIMD 2020v2 glossary; reviewed (AI-assisted review, 2026-10-02, record))
  • Mortality (HlthSMR, standardised ratio; SIMD 2020v2 glossary; reviewed (AI-assisted review, 2026-10-02, record))
  • Proportion of population being prescribed drugs for anxiety, depression or psychosis (HlthDprsPc, percentage; SIMD 2020v2 glossary; reviewed (AI-assisted review, 2026-10-02, record))
  • Proportion of live singleton births of low birth weight (HlthLBWTPc, percentage; SIMD 2020v2 glossary; reviewed (AI-assisted review, 2026-10-02, record))
  • Emergency stays in hospital (HlthEmerSR, standardised ratio; SIMD 2020v2 glossary; reviewed (AI-assisted review, 2026-10-02, record))
Table Type Nullable Category In the CSV export SQL Server type history table (postcode_simd_history, SPD) int8 no computed population-weighted domain band yes tinyint main table (postcode_simd, SSPL) int8 no computed population-weighted domain band yes tinyint

docs.title: Provenance (the same in both tables)
docs.text:
Each table runs its own copy of the table-level checks, named .history. and .main..

Where it comes from

Input Field Condition Reaches the row by data.gov.uk/SG_SIMD_2020/SG_SIMD_2020.dbf (pinned, SHA256 3eb0f27aa4aa…) hlthrank: Health domain rank (SIMD 2020v2 glossary; reviewed (AI-assisted review, 2026-10-02, record)) every data zone of the edition DataZone2011Code = datazone data.gov.uk/SG_SIMD_2020/SG_SIMD_2020.dbf (pinned, SHA256 3eb0f27aa4aa…) sape2017: 2017 NRS small area population estimates (SIMD 2020v2 glossary; reviewed (AI-assisted review, 2026-10-02, record)) every data zone of the edition DataZone2011Code = datazone

Scope: every data zone of SIMD 2020v2, once, with its population; never the table's rows.

What was done to it: computed. Zones ordered by the domain rank, equal ranks one block; band = max(1, min(10, ceil(midpoint x 10 / total))), where midpoint is the cumulative population through the block minus half the block's. How it is checked (what each check tests; whether a build passed it is in that build's manifest.json["checks"])

  • weighted.2020v2.zones: the population is joined to every PHS zone of the edition
  • weighted.2020v2.reproduces_phs_scotland_decile: the population midpoint rule reproduces PHS's published overall Scotland band on every zone
  • join.<table>.simd2020v2_health_domain_pw_scotland_decile.range: every joined band is within its range
  • readback.<table>.attached_values: every attached value in the saved file is looked up again from the sources and equal

Why: computed-weighted-domain-bands

docs.title: asset-naming
docs.text:
Date: 2026-09-10. Status: implemented.

Decision. The two reference tables are named phs_bands and govscot_bands. The joined output is postcode_simd and the directory table is postcode_index.

Reason. The pair of names states the one thing an analyst must not confuse, which publisher's weighting a band carries. Grain-based names distinguished nothing, since both tables are keyed by edition and data zone.

Evidence. Step 2 review, 10 September 2026. Renamed before the first release so the instance record starts with the final keys.

docs.title: band-column-names-state-weighting
docs.text:
Date: 2026-09-10. Status: implemented.

Decision. PHS population-weighted bands are named simd{ed}pw; Scottish Government unweighted bands are simd{ed}uw.

Reason. The PHS guidance says the two must never be mixed in one analysis and must always be identified. A column name is the label an analyst cannot lose.

Evidence. PHS deprivation guidance v3.5, section 3.1.1 and checklist.

Columns (78): simd2004_least15pc, simd2004_most15pc, simd2004_pw_ca_decile, simd2004_pw_ca_quintile, simd2004_pw_hb_decile, simd2004_pw_hb_quintile, simd2004_pw_hscp_decile, simd2004_pw_hscp_quintile, docs.title: cli-first
docs.text:
Date: 2026-09-12. Status: implemented.

Decision. The CLI is the only build path. Remove the Dagster runtime, web server, asset wrappers, instance configuration and persisted intermediates. Keep one visible verify/prepare/cross-check/join/readback/publish sequence, a human build report and small retained run records.

Reason. Routine maintenance is a postcode-directory refresh; SIMD editions arrive less frequently. A full deterministic rebuild from pinned sources is cheap. Source/configuration snapshots, runtime/code hashes and saved-file checks provide lineage without a second execution model.

Evidence. tests/test_pipeline.py tests postcode refresh, full replacement, failure evidence, read-only audit and a synthetic seventh edition on a new data-zone vintage.

docs.title: computed-weighted-domain-bands
docs.text:
Date: 2026-10-01. Status: implemented.

Decision. Both tables carry a computed population-weighted Scotland quintile and decile of every domain rank, simd_domain_pw_scotland, 82 columns, and each edition's data-zone population, simdpopulation, 6 columns: schemas postcode_simd_wide_v5 (442) and postcode_simd_sspl_v5 (399). The one exception to bands-are-looked-up: nobody publishes these. They are cut per data zone in the Government reader, every zone of the edition once with that edition's shapefile population, never from a postcode table: zones ordered by rank, equal ranks one block, band = max(1, min(k, ceil(midpoint * k / total))). Before any is used, the same rule must reproduce PHS's published overall Scotland quintile and decile exactly in every edition, or the build stops. Labelled "computed population-weighted band, using a midpoint rule validated against PHS's published overall bands; equal ranks grouped together; not published by PHS or the Government". SQL measures computed_pwdomain; the walkthrough carries the decile beside the published one. Scotland only; no sub-geography bands, flags or vigintiles. Released as 6.0.0.

Reason. Analysts ask for population-weighted domain bands, and official guidance recommends the income domain alone, or SIMD without health, for health outcomes; the Scottish Government's income-employment index and Bradford et al. (Health & Place, 2023) cut population-based bands of domain measures. Checking the rule against PHS on every build is what makes a computed band defensible. PHS is to be asked whether it has a view; the attribution stays "computed" unless it does.

Evidence. The rule reproduces PHS's published Scotland quintile and decile on every zone of all six editions; within health boards, HSCPs and councils it does not, mostly in the island areas, so none are produced. Every computed band holds its fifth or tenth of the population to within 0.036 percentage points. Cutting from the main table's zones instead would drop four 2011 zones (801 people in 2017) and change five 2020v2 income deciles. The 354 history and 311 main columns of 5.0.0 keep their fingerprints. Plan: docs/plans/Weighted_Domain_Bands_Plan.md.

docs.title: database-load-check
docs.text:
Date: 2026-09-16. Status: implemented.

Decision. Two more generated scripts ship beside the lookups, both produced by python -m simd_ingest.sql_check from the output schemas and the export contract. docs/sql/import_csv.sql stages each shared CSV as text and restores the declared types, putting an empty cell back as a blank or a null according to the contract's rules. docs/sql/check_loaded_digest.sql then verifies the declared columns, types, nullability and order, the natural key, the absence of the characters the digest frames with, the row count and the row digest the build recorded. Expected values come from the manifest, never from the loaded table. The scripts read; they never repair, replace or promote anything, and the CLI never connects to a database.

Reason. A file hash proves the CSV arrived intact, not that the load preserved it, and the two failures that matter are silent: a reader gives every empty field as NULL whatever it meant, and an empty string becomes 1900-01-01 as a datetime. The digest is computed from the accepted table rather than from a re-read of the file, so an import mistake cannot appear on both sides of the comparison. It is compact and probabilistic: each SHA-256 is truncated to eight bytes and the signed prefixes are summed, so collisions and cancelling changes are possible. It detects accidental corruption and is neither an exact cell comparison nor a signature. Structure and key checks sit beside it because a digest is order independent and blind to types.

Evidence. Verified on SQL Server 2022 Developer Edition 16.0.4252.3 in the project's container. Both tables imported by the shipped recipe, 230,103 and 247,773 rows, and all ten checks passed with the digests equal to the manifest's. Eight deliberate corruptions were each caught and undone: a lost leading zero, a blank turned into a null and the reverse, an empty deletion date turned into 1900-01-01, truncated text, a changed band away from any documented example, a deleted row, and a column altered to accept null. The five lookup queries ran there unchanged and gave their documented answers, which retires the "SQL Server syntax intended but not verified" caveat for that version only. Findings recorded in the recipe: CODEPAGE is rejected on Linux, so the encoding is declared as a UTF-8 collation on the staging columns; HASHBYTES over an nvarchar expression hashes UTF-16, so the text is converted to varchar with a binary UTF-8 collation first; and CONCAT_WS drops a NULL argument, so every column is wrapped before framing.

Reason. A clean-machine reproduction on demand, and one artefact HIC can run without assembling a Python environment. Where the image is published is still to be decided.

docs.text:
Date: 2026-09-12. Status: implemented.

Decision. PHS header order, data-zone vintage, band direction and Government column maps are declared per edition. Both publishers must declare the same edition keys, vintage and zone count. Add explicit output fields for each new edition, and PHS geography fields for new vintages; shared-vintage geography must agree. Analyst edition-by-year recommendations are reviewed separately.

Reason. New editions using the supported CSV/DBF layout need registry and schema changes, not a new build path. Unknown formats or incomplete historical geography coverage require deliberate review.

Decision. The Scottish Government unweighted quintile, decile and vigintile come from the six maps.gov.scot shapefile attribute tables, joined on data zone, one route for every edition.

Date: 2026-09-10. Status: implemented.

Decision. A record is valid for introduced_on <= date < deleted_on, with null deletion open-ended. Same-day records are retained but never match an as-of query.

Reason. Eight small-user records reuse 18 February 2026 as both a deletion and a reintroduction date, so a closed-interval rule would report overlaps that are not there.

docs.text:
Date: 2026-09-10. Status: superseded.

Decision. The Dagster instance, which is the provenance record, lives at .dagster inside the project and is backed up together with results/. Intermediate tables are kept outside it under data/work.

Reason. A record in a temporary path is not a record. Whether HIC wants it on a shared, backed-up path instead is an operational decision still to be taken; it is one environment variable either way.

docs.title: invert-2004-2006-phs-bands
docs.text:
Date: 2026-09-09. Status: implemented.

Decision. The eight PHS population-weighted bands for SIMD 2004 and 2006 are re-derived as 11 - decile and 6 - quintile so that 1 means most deprived in every edition. Ranks and the Most15pc and Least15pc flags are never inverted.

Reason. PHS publishes those two editions with 1 = least deprived, the reverse of every later edition. The PHS deprivation guidance requires the reversal to be handled; handling it once upstream prevents every analyst handling it separately.

Evidence. PHS 2004 rank 1 has published country decile 10 and official government decile 1. Reversal is exactly invertible; raw files are pinned.

docs.title: large-user-geography-attached
docs.text:
Date: 2026-09-10. Status: implemented.

Decision. SIMD is attached to every large-user record, including PO boxes, because the directory assigns them a data zone. This is ingestion source fidelity, not a claim about residence eligibility. Default SSPL SQL preserves own-record values and flags address concerns; legacy SPD SQL follows links. Python keeps its own-record geography and sentinel exclusion. See sspl-direct-sql-both-publishers.

Reason. Source fidelity. The build attaches what the directory says; it does not decide which postcodes deserve a value.

Evidence. PHS deprivation guidance v3.5, Appendix A.

docs.title: link-sentinels
docs.text:
Date: 2026-09-10. Status: implemented.

Decision. NO LINKP and NO LINK in the large-user linked-postcode field are kept as text and both classified as no link. Ingestion attaches SIMD through each record's own data zone, not through this field. Default SSPL SQL preserves those values with address warnings; only legacy SPD SQL follows links. See sspl-direct-sql-both-publishers.

Reason. NO LINKP is documented for PO boxes. NO LINK is undocumented and appears on six deleted records.

Evidence. 31,725 NO LINKP, 6 NO LINK, 19,273 real links, all resolving.

docs.title: linkage-by-era
docs.text:
Date: 2026-09-11. Status: superseded.

Decision. Linking events to SIMD by era follows the guidance's table 4, each event taking the edition recommended for its year and the record valid on its date. Events before 1996 get status no_edition with every SIMD column null, including the matched key. The Python and SQL implementations are tested to agree row for row on a synthetic cohort.

Reason. One rule, two implementations that cannot drift. Withholding the key on no_edition keeps the output columns consistent: no edition, no answer.

Evidence. tests/test_lookup.py ByEraPythonAndSqlAgree; docs/sql/link_by_era.sql; docs/LINKAGE_BY_ERA.md.

docs.title: lookup-statuses
docs.text:
Date: 2026-09-11. Status: superseded.

Decision. simd_ingest.lookup resolves a postcode to one of five statuses, unique, split_consensus, split_conflict, deleted or not_found. Several valid records agree on the requested measure gives consensus with the value; disagreement gives conflict with a null value. A full NRS key selects its own split part. Never choose A, average or vote.

Reason. The policy already agreed in the plan, made executable. Ambiguity is reported, not hidden.

Evidence. On the 226 current ordinary postcodes with more than one record, rank gives 203 conflicts and 23 consensus; docs/EXAMPLES.md.

docs.title: lookups-exclude-po-boxes
docs.text:
Date: 2026-09-11. Status: superseded.

Decision. Every lookup, in Python and in the SQL, excludes large-user records whose link field is NO LINKP or NO LINK by default. Both offer a switch to include them, and a second switch to exclude all large-user records. The table itself keeps every record with the SIMD the directory assigns.

Reason. The PHS guidance, Appendix A, attaches no deprivation to PO boxes because their location is a sorting office. An analyst reading the guidance expects the default to match it; the table stays source-faithful because the exclusion is applied at lookup time, not at build time.

Evidence. 1,518 current PO box records among 4,767 current large-user records.

docs.title: nullable-integers-and-never-blank-text
docs.text:
Date: 2026-09-21. Status: implemented.

Decision. The writers now carry two kinds of column the tables never had. A nullable integer is written to Parquet as a null, rendered in the CSV as an empty cell and in the digest as the null marker, and restored on import with NULLIF, never as zero. A nullable text column that is never blank is named under empty_is_null in the export contract, and the import restores its empty cells as nulls; every other text column keeps its existing rule, blank or structural null by record type.

Reason. The rurality codes are the first nullable integers and their statuses the first text that is either a value or null. Without the rules an empty code would load as 0, a class that does not exist, and an empty status would load as a blank, which the digest would then report as corruption of a faithful load.

Evidence. Verified on SQL Server 2022 (16.0, RTM-CU24-GDR) in the local container with the shipped import and check scripts: 230,103 and 247,773 rows, all ten checks pass, history digest -3244194952865985434297 over 185 exported columns equal to the manifest's. The main table's digest, 600732040592218046898, is unchanged. tests/test_exports.py requires the NULLIF guard on every nullable integer and the rule on every empty_is_null column.

Columns (27): urbanrural2003_2004_6fold, urbanrural2003_2004_8fold, urbanrural2003_2004_status, urbanrural2005_2006_6fold, urbanrural2005_2006_8fold, urbanrural2005_2006_status, urbanrural2007_2008_6fold, urbanrural2007_2008_8fold, urbanrural2007_2008_status, urbanrural2009_2010_6fold, urbanrural2009_2010_8fold, urbanrural2009_2010_status, urbanrural2011_2012_6fold, urbanrural2011_2012_8fold, urbanrural2011_2012_status, urbanrural2013_2014_6fold, urbanrural2013_2014_8fold, urbanrural2013_2014_status, urbanrural2016_6fold, urbanrural2016_8fold, urbanrural2016_status, urbanrural2020_6fold, urbanrural2020_8fold, urbanrural2020_status, urbanrural2022_6fold, urbanrural2022_8fold, urbanrural2022_status

docs.title: patient-linkage-deferred
docs.text:
Date: 2026-09-10. Status: superseded.

Decision. The downstream resolver for ambiguous split postcodes, with its unique, split_consensus, split_conflict, incomplete and not_found statuses, is recorded in the plan and not implemented here.

Reason. It belongs to the consumer of this table, not to its ingestion.

docs.title: percentile-omitted
docs.text:
Date: 2026-09-10. Status: implemented.

Decision. No percentile column in any edition.

Reason. No source publishes a stable percentile for 2001 data zones. The shapefile tables carry one, but it follows neither band rule and differs between editions. Filling two editions and leaving four null would invite misuse.

Evidence. SIMD_Source_API_Options.md.

docs.title: phs-geography-columns
docs.text:
Date: 2026-09-10. Status: implemented.

Decision. Six columns carry the health board, HSCP and council area code PHS assigned to each data zone, one set per data-zone vintage.

Reason. The within-geography bands are only valid against the geography PHS computed them in, which differs from the directory's 2019 code on a few records.

Evidence. 8 records differ for 2011 zones; 35 (HB) and 86 (HSCP, CA) for 2001 zones. PHS codes are identical across editions of the same vintage.

docs.title: postcode-normalisation
docs.text:
Date: 2026-09-09. Status: implemented.

Decision. pc_norm is the postcode uppercased with ASCII spaces removed, keeping any NRS split suffix. pc_base removes a validated A, B or C suffix only from a small-user record flagged as split. A large-user split flag never shortens its own postcode.

Reason. The suffix attaches to bases of five to seven characters, so length alone cannot identify it. A large-user split flag describes its linked small-user postcode.

Evidence. 458 current small-user split records, all ending in A, B or C; 226 ordinary postcodes with more than one current candidate.

Columns (1): pc_norm

docs.title: previous-life-fallback
docs.text:
Date: 2026-09-23. Status: implemented.

Decision. When no postcode life contains the address date but the postcode had a life that ended before it, the dated SQL query, the walkthrough and the Python dated lookups use that life: the one whose deletion date is the latest on or before the address date, excluding same-day records, and never a later life. The row reports postcode_status previous_life, or in Python status previous_life, which carries SIMD and rurality like matched. Every rule that applies to a record still applies: a retired PO box gets nothing, and a retired large user's linked small-user record must be valid on the last day of the life used. The context columns first_introduced_on, previous_life_deleted_on and next_life_introduced_on are unchanged, so the gap and any reissue stay visible. between_lives and postcode_deleted_by_date remain for the case where only same-day records ended before the date. No gap tolerance is applied.

Reason. A record carrying a postcode after its retirement is most often a Royal Mail recoding the record never caught up with: the building did not move, so the retired postcode's last location is where the person lived. The latest-life queries already gave retired postcodes their last life's SIMD, so the dated query was stricter than its siblings by accident rather than by design. Reporting a status of its own keeps the choice reviewable and lets an analyst exclude it with one filter. A later life is excluded because a reissue can be anywhere.

Evidence. On the built table: G3 8NR, retired July 2015 and reissued in a different data zone in January 2018, asked for June 2016 returns its 1978 life in S01010278, quintile 1, not the reissue's S01010283, quintile 4. FK17 8DS in its 1978 gap returns its 1973 life, and TD9 7PQ, retired in 1999, returns its only life for 2020. tests/test_sql_sets.py and tests/test_lookup.py cover the gap, the date after the last life, three lives with two gaps, a same-day record, a retired PO box, and a retired large user whose link ended the same day or earlier; the walkthrough agrees with the generated query. This changes what the dated SQL and the Python dated lookups return for those rows, and is part of the 3.0.0 release.

docs.title: python-lookups-choose-then-exclude
docs.text:
Date: 2026-09-23. Status: implemented.

Decision. The Python lookups choose the record first, on the whole table, and apply the PO-box and large-user exclusions to the record chosen. A date that an excluded record covers is not_found; it is never answered by an older life. The shared resolver takes several value columns and resolves them as one tuple from one record, a null counting as a value, so a rurality class and its stored reason can never come from different split parts. attach_by_era and attach_rurality reassemble the cohort by position, not index label, and accept an empty cohort. A row with no date gets missing_date in attach, attach_by_era and attach_rurality, rather than deleted, no_edition or before_first_version.

Reason. Review of 9fa39d4 found four faults, all in Python and none in SQL. Excluding PO boxes before choosing the life let the previous-life fallback answer AB10 1WS in 2025 from a 1996 life although a PO-box life covers that date; the SQL chooses the life first and returns no value. Resolving a class and its reason separately, with nulls ignored in the agreement check, gave HS6 5HT class 6 beside outside_polygons and PA66 6BN not_found although both of its parts exist. Label-based reassembly duplicated rows sharing an index label and failed on an empty cohort. A missing date read as a date before the first edition or version. The last two were already in attach_by_era on main.

Evidence. On the built table: AB10 1WS on 2025-01-01 is not_found, and unique with its own value only when PO boxes are asked for; HS6 5HT in 2005-2006 is split_conflict under the report rule and the A part, class 6, by default, as in SQL; PA66 6BN is outside_polygons under both rules. tests/test_lookup.py pins each fault on a small table and the reviewer's postcodes on the built one. No SQL, schema or built data changed.

docs.title: rank-direction-confirmed
docs.text:
Date: 2026-09-10. Status: implemented.

Decision. Rank 1 is the most deprived data zone in all six editions.

Reason. The PHS rank is identical to the official Scottish Government rank on every zone in every edition, which contradicts the PHS documentation sentence about 2004 and 2006.

Evidence. SIMD_Plan_Gap_Closure.md section 4.

docs.title: recommended-edition-is-explicit
docs.text:
Date: 2026-09-11. Status: implemented.

Decision. lookup.recommended_edition implements the PHS guidance's table 4, years of health data to edition. Nothing calls it implicitly; the analyst passes an edition to every lookup.

Reason. Which edition to use is the analyst's decision under the guidance. The helper makes the recommendation easy to follow and impossible to follow by accident.

docs.title: reconstruction-is-diagnostic
docs.text:
Date: 2026-09-10. Status: superseded.

Decision. Reconstructing the PHS population-weighted bands from ranks and population is a diagnostic that never blocks a build and never replaces a published value.

Reason. The ingestion guarantee is source fidelity, not reproduction of the publisher's method.

Evidence. The midpoint rule reproduces every Scotland-level decile and quintile in all six editions; three 15% flag cells and two Shetland sub-geography zones differ. Expected exceptions are pinned in acceptance_baselines.yaml.

docs.title: record-key
docs.text:
Date: 2026-09-10. Status: implemented.

Decision. The primary key is normalised postcode plus introduction date. Deletion date, user type and release are attributes.

Reason. Unique across all 247,773 records in SPD 2026/2. Postcode alone repeats up to seven times.

Evidence. SIMD_Plan_Gap_Closure.md section 6. Validated on every release; never silently deduplicated.

docs.title: release-facts-not-fixed-gates
docs.text:
Date: 2026-09-12. Status: implemented.

Decision. Published file/all/live/deleted counts remain blocking inputs in sources.yaml. Header contracts remain explicit. Split/repeated-key/key-length/touching-date/link-category/ambiguity profiles are recorded observations, not fixed 2026/2 acceptance constants. Compare each new snapshot with the previous hash-verified snapshot by natural key, excluding the release label from record changes.

Reason. Normal release changes should be visible to a reviewer without requiring changes to pipeline code or weakening correctness checks. An unavailable comparison is reported explicitly and does not block a source-faithful build.

docs.title: rurality-by-version
docs.text:
Date: 2026-09-21. Status: implemented.

Decision. The history table carries the Scottish Government Urban Rural Classification of all nine published versions, 2003-2004 to 2022, for every postcode life: per version a 6-fold and an 8-fold code and a status, 27 nullable columns appended to the 162 of postcode_simd_wide_v1, which are unchanged and in the same order. The schema becomes postcode_simd_wide_v2. Each life's own grid reference is placed in that version's pinned polygons (core/rurality.py). A point in no polygon is null with status outside_polygons, with no nearest-polygon fallback. A point on an edge between two classes is null with ambiguous_polygons. A post-office box, a large user linked NO LINKP, is null in every version with status po_box, because NRS puts its grid reference at the sorting or delivery office. The two 2022 columns NRS publishes are kept exactly as supplied; the derived 2022 columns sit beside them. The main table is unchanged: SSPL allocates from output-area centroids and keeps one life per postcode, so it has no per-life point.

Reason. The directory carries one classification, the 2022 one, so a historical address was described by today's categories while its data zone and SIMD were read at the right vintage. About one life in nine has a different 6-fold class in a version before 2020 than the 2022 code it carries. Every version's polygons are still published, so one postcode file and one method give every version without archived lookups. The status is stored per row because a null can mean three different things and a count in the build report cannot say which rows. Keeping the published columns beside the derived ones leaves the validation permanently visible rather than overwriting a publisher's value.

Evidence. Gate fixed before the run at 99.5% for current small users and 99% for other cohorts over 1,000 lives: point-in-polygon on the 2022 polygons reproduces NRS's published 2022 codes on 247,770 of 247,773 lives, 100% of current lives, and all three misses are deleted lives outside every polygon, none a different class. In the built table the derived 2022 codes equal the published ones on all 216,045 placed rows; 31,725 boxes are withheld; outside_polygons is 3 to 34 per version except 767 non-box lives in 2005-2006, whose coastline is drawn tighter. The original 162 columns keep fingerprint 59369357e44e45a5, now pinned as wide_v1_columns_fingerprint; the main table keeps 9515021d99099b43. Readback places every point again from the saved grid references, and a test changes a 2005-2006 code, a 2013-2014 code and a 2022 status after writing and requires each to be caught. Plan and feasibility result: docs/plans/Rurality_By_Version_Plan.md.

Columns (27): urbanrural2003_2004_6fold, urbanrural2003_2004_8fold, urbanrural2003_2004_status, urbanrural2005_2006_6fold, urbanrural2005_2006_8fold, urbanrural2005_2006_status, urbanrural2007_2008_6fold, urbanrural2007_2008_8fold, urbanrural2007_2008_status, urbanrural2009_2010_6fold, urbanrural2009_2010_8fold, urbanrural2009_2010_status, urbanrural2011_2012_6fold, urbanrural2011_2012_8fold, urbanrural2011_2012_status, urbanrural2013_2014_6fold, urbanrural2013_2014_8fold, urbanrural2013_2014_status, urbanrural2016_6fold, urbanrural2016_8fold, urbanrural2016_status, urbanrural2020_6fold, urbanrural2020_8fold, urbanrural2020_status, urbanrural2022_6fold, urbanrural2022_8fold, urbanrural2022_status

docs.title: rurality-early-versions-confirmed
docs.text:
Date: 2026-09-25. Status: implemented.

Decision. The four Urban Rural Classification versions not linked from the catalogue record, 2003-2004, 2005-2006, 2007-2008 and 2009-2010, stay in the registry and in the history table on the same footing as the five catalogued ones. Version by reference year remains a project choice.

Reason. They were found at the publisher's own download address but are absent from the catalogue record, so their standing needed confirming before they supported historical analysis. The publisher has now confirmed it.

Evidence. Email reply from the Scottish Government's Rural Statistics team, 25 September 2026, to a query sent to RuralStatistics@gov.scot with GI-SAT@gov.scot copied. Having consulted colleagues, they confirmed that the four versions, under the same Open Government Licence, are the most appropriate ones for the relevant time periods; that they encourage the most recent version in general but that previous versions are appropriate for historical analysis; and that there were no major methodological changes making the versions not comparable. The reply did not address reference year against publication date.

docs.title: rurality-version-by-reference-year
docs.text:
Date: 2026-09-21. Status: implemented.

Decision. The three SPD queries and the walkthrough return the Urban Rural Classification version that suits the year, as rurality_version, rurality_policy, rurality_6fold, rurality_8fold and rurality_status, placed after the shared 41-column core. The version is chosen by reference year, the year it describes, and applies until the year before the next version: 2003-2004, 2005-2006, 2007-2008, 2009-2010, 2011-2012, 2013 to 2015, 2016 to 2019, 2020 to 2021, 2022 onwards. The year is the one that chose the SIMD edition, so an overriding analysis_year fixes both. link_latest.sql uses the latest version throughout. The codes are the matched record's own. rurality_status reports a postcode status where no single record stands for the postcode, then missing_year, before_first_version or invalid_year, then the reason stored with the record. The windows are generated from the registry's reference years. The SSPL set is unchanged.

Reason. PHS publishes no equivalent of Table 4 for rurality, so this is a project choice and is labelled as one in the queries and their output. Reference year rather than publication date because the purpose is to describe where a person lived, not what was knowable when: by publication date, events from 2022 to most of 2024 would take the 2020 version, since the 2022 version appeared on 16 December 2024. A separate status is needed because the SIMD status cannot express these outcomes: 1996 has a SIMD edition and no rurality version.

Evidence. gov.scot: Urban Rural Classification 2022 published 16 December 2024, built on the Census 2022 settlements. Output columns: SSPL 89 unchanged, SPD era and latest 108, SPD as-of 111. tests/test_sql_sets.py states the versions and the year windows independently of the generator and checks fourteen years, the statuses, a large user reporting its own class while its SIMD comes from its link, and that the SSPL set has no rurality column. The walkthrough agrees with the generated query on the four rurality columns across fifteen cases on the built table.

docs.title: shared-exports
docs.text:
Date: 2026-09-16. Status: implemented.

Decision. Every build writes a gzipped CSV of each table beside the Parquet, and one contract, simd_ingest/export_contract.yaml, governs both it and the SQL examples. The contract withholds GridReferenceEasting and GridReferenceNorthing from both tables and Latitude and Longitude from the history table, so neither the CSV nor a linkage result carries a coordinate; the Parquet keeps every column and its schemas are unchanged. CSV is comma separated with RFC 4180 quoting, UTF-8 without a byte order mark, LF endings and gzip written with no name or timestamp, so the same rows give the same bytes. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD, is_current is 1 or 0, and all other values are written exactly as stored. A null and a source blank are the same empty cell, resolved by table, column and record type, which the dictionaries state and the contract records. The build also records a row digest per table, computed from the accepted table rather than from a re-read of the file, so a database load can be checked after import. Each CSV is read back cell for cell before publication; results/CSV_README.txt carries every publisher's attribution; the manifest is written last and records every hash; audit recomputes them.

Reason. The CSV is how the table is shown to the team, so it is the copy most likely to leave the building and the one that should carry the least. Withholding coordinates is a project data-minimisation choice first: a linkage result is one row per patient, and a grid reference is a precise location where a data zone is not. It is also conservative about licensing, since NRS restricts "postcode boundaries and grid references" separately from its openly licensed index and lookups but does not say which governs a coordinate column inside an index file. That reading is unconfirmed and is on the list of questions for Research Data Scotland. Excluding the columns from the SQL as well keeps one policy rather than a footgun for anyone who imports the CSV under the table name the queries use.

Evidence. tests/test_exports.py states the renderings independently of the writer and covers the empty-cell rules, leading zeros, quoting, non-ASCII and supplementary characters, determinism, structural damage and the corruptions a load introduces. Reserved framing characters are rejected in source text rather than stripped. On SPD 2026/2 and SSPL 2026/2 the CSVs are 8.3 MB and 7.2 MB gzipped, and both rows-only fingerprints are unchanged; the Parquet file hashes change because this entry changes the decision log.

docs.title: simd-domain-bands
docs.text:
Date: 2026-09-30. Status: implemented.

Decision. Both tables carry the Scottish Government's published quintile, decile and vigintile of every domain rank, for every edition, simd_domain, copied from three statistics.gov.scot datasets (2004 to 2012, 2016, 2020) and never derived, as for every band (bands-are-looked-up). The ranks stay from the shapefiles. A band is admitted only where its dataset's rank is the shapefile's: equal, or a half rank the 2004 to 2012 dataset rounds up, or one of the 628 2020v2 housing zones pinned with both ranks in simd_ingest/sgs_2020_housing_rank_disagreements.csv; anything else stops the build. Those 628 zones carry simd2020v2_housing_domain_rank_source_status = rank_sources_disagree: the two Government publications disagree on the rank; it is not a statement that the band is wrong. 123 band columns and the status, appended after every existing column: schemas postcode_simd_wide_v4 (354) and postcode_simd_sspl_v4 (311). The SQL core grows from 48 to 70 columns and never counts the status as missing; Python returns the answering record's status for housing, and split parts reach consensus only if they agree on both the value and the status. Unweighted and Scotland only. Released as 5.0.0.

Reason. The Government publishes domain bands for every edition, so a derived band would be a second, competing version: no rule on the rank alone reproduces all of them, since the publisher splits some ties across adjacent bands and placed the same 2016 and 2020 tie differently. Copying keeps the publisher's value, and checking the ranks keeps each band tied to the ranking we carry. The SIMD team has been asked which 2020 housing ranking is authoritative; the feature does not wait for the answer.

Evidence. The vintage band rules reproduce all 18 published overall series and PHS's weighted Scotland bands for all six editions, but against the 819,897 published domain bands the best rank-only rule disagrees in 19. Split ties: 2006 income and employment, 2009 employment (S01001951 and S01006050, both 1952, deciles 3 and 4). The 2790.5 housing pair S01008149 and S01012978 is decile 5 in 2016 and 4 in 2020. 2020 housing ranks differ in 628 zones by 0.5 to 4.5 places, S01008634 2093 against 2092.5; under the 2020 convention that changes a band in two zones only. The overall index agrees in both publications for every edition and zone. The datasets are byte-identical across downloads. The 230 history and 187 main columns of 4.0.0 keep their fingerprints. Plans: docs/plans/Domain_Ntiles_Test_Plan.md and docs/plans/Domain_Bands_Plan.md. Answered 2 October 2026 by the Scottish Government's SIMD team (email to Michele Tinti): the SIMD 2020v2 ranks workbook is the definitive version, the differences are too small to worry about, and are probably due to how ties were treated. The ranks we carry equal the workbook in every zone, so the status marks zones where statistics.gov.scot departs from the definitive ranking. Our check of the explanation: 115 of the 628 zones are tied in neither ranking, and the largest tied group among them has six zones, which cannot account for a 4.5-place difference, so ties explain only part; the effect remains two band changes, no quintile. No change to the build.

docs.title: simd-domain-ranks
docs.text:
Date: 2026-09-29. Status: implemented.

Decision. Both tables carry the Scottish Government's published SIMD domain ranks for every edition, simd_domain_rank for income, employment, health, education, access, crime and housing, copied exactly as published and appended after every existing column: 41 columns, schemas postcode_simd_wide_v3 and postcode_simd_sspl_v3. 2004 published no crime domain and has no crime column. A new schema type, rank, keeps a value that may end in .5 exactly: float64 in Parquet, one decimal place in the CSV, decimal(6,1) in SQL Server and in the digest, a float in Python, never an integer anywhere. The registry's domains map per government edition is the single statement of which domain exists in which edition; the reader, join, readback, trace, SQL generator and Python API all read it. The SQL output core grows from 41 to 48 columns with seven gov_domain_rank measures; for an edition that did not publish a domain the measure is null and the result is still matched. Python answers an unpublished domain with a null value and a label, not an error. Ranks only: no domain bands or n-tiles. Released as 4.0.0. The published domain bands were added, copied, never derived, by simd-domain-bands on 30 September 2026.

Reason. The HEAL-Scot DRS asks for domain-level data and other projects will. The ranks were already pinned in the Government shapefile attribute tables. They are not whole numbers, and ties are only mostly averaged, so they are copied rather than recomputed, and every layer is held to exactness. The new columns change both schemas, the CSV digest and the loader's expectations, the same reasoning that made the rurality work 3.0.0.

Evidence. 7,796 published domain-rank values end in .5, for example 2020v2 income for S01006523 is 5955.5; of 5,188 tied groups 4,116 carry their average position and 1,072 do not, such as 2009 income 5521 and 2020v2 income 6969. Every value is a whole multiple of 0.5. The saved 2020v2 ranks equal the Government's SIMD 2020v2 ranks workbook, a retired pin, on all 6,976 zones in all seven domains. The 189 existing history columns keep fingerprint ddb162ef89c7d52a and the 146 existing main columns 9515021d99099b43, both now pinned. Plan and review: docs/plans/Domain_Ranks_Plan.md.

Columns (41): simd2004_access_domain_rank, simd2004_education_domain_rank, simd2004_employment_domain_rank, simd2004_health_domain_rank, simd2004_housing_domain_rank, simd2004_income_domain_rank, simd2006_access_domain_rank, simd2006_crime_domain_rank, simd2006_education_domain_rank, simd2006_employment_domain_rank, simd2006_health_domain_rank, simd2006_housing_domain_rank, simd2006_income_domain_rank, simd2009v2_access_domain_rank, simd2009v2_crime_domain_rank, simd2009v2_education_domain_rank, simd2009v2_employment_domain_rank, simd2009v2_health_domain_rank, simd2009v2_housing_domain_rank, simd2009v2_income_domain_rank, simd2012_access_domain_rank, simd2012_crime_domain_rank, simd2012_education_domain_rank, simd2012_employment_domain_rank, simd2012_health_domain_rank, simd2012_housing_domain_rank, simd2012_income_domain_rank, simd2016_access_domain_rank, simd2016_crime_domain_rank, simd2016_education_domain_rank, simd2016_employment_domain_rank, simd2016_health_domain_rank, simd2016_housing_domain_rank, simd2016_income_domain_rank, simd2020v2_access_domain_rank, simd2020v2_crime_domain_rank, simd2020v2_education_domain_rank, simd2020v2_employment_domain_rank, simd2020v2_health_domain_rank, simd2020v2_housing_domain_rank, simd2020v2_income_domain_rank

docs.text:
Date: 2026-09-12. Status: implemented.

Decision. Use one writer per results directory. Validate the saved candidate and prepare evidence before individually replacing the current table and sidecars. Reason. Atomic replacement protects the table from validation failures. It is not a transaction across the table and sidecars; their hash agreement must be checked before import.
